newsitem.title: USA: Oakley sees new lines helping sales.
newsitem.headline: Oakley sees new lines helping sales.

text.p: Eyewear maker Oakley Inc said Thursday it expects to benefit in the 1997 second half from new lines like its Topcoat sunglasses, following poor sales during the first half.

"Although we are disappointed with our sales results, we are encouraged by the very positive response we have experienced at retail for the new Fives and polarized products which launched in the quarter," it said in a statement.
Oakley said it planned to release the Topcoat line next month.
The eyewear maker reported lower sales and earnings for the second quarter and first half.

"Domestic sales declined as a result of significantly lower sales to Sunglass Hut, the company's largest customer, but reflected the increasing benefits of Oakley's accelerated product introductions and efforts to diversify the domestic retail account base," it said.
Domestic sales made up $35.1 million of the total $55.2 million of sales for the second quarter.

"International sales reflected modest growth in the company's European operations, a decrease in sales to a limited number of large distributors, and lower sales in Japan and South Africa, where the company recently converted to direct sales operations," it said.
"Despite the short-term impact in these new direct markets, the company believes the changes that have been implemented should lay the foundation for long-term growth," it added.
